text: (hopefully) shouldn’t encounter , , let us explain: Basically default setting communicating EyeLink machine filtering enabled either live-streamed data saved data EDF files. want filters ’s unclear low-pass filter specifications, conflicts assumption eyeris::detransient() use one-step difference compute threshold detecting large jumps pupil data (suggesting blinking artifacts). general, ’d like data raw possible can “cook” fresh. , data aren’t raw possible, need run eyeris without detransient step. skip detransient step, pass skip_detransient = TRUE glassbox() call.
code: ***WARNING: SOMETHING OUTRAGEOUS IS HAPPENING WITH YOUR PUPIL DATA!***   The median absolute deviation (MAD) of your pupil speed is 0.  This indicates a potential setup / hardware issue which has likely propogated into your pupil recording.  Most often, this is due to online filtering being applied directly to your pupil data via the EyeLink Host PC.   WE DO NOT RECOMMEND USING ANY ONLINE AUTO FILTERING DURING YOUR DATA RECORDING.   ***ADDITIONAL INFO*** The default setting for communicating with the EyeLink  machine is to have filtering enabled on either live-streamed data or saved data in EDF files.   We do not want these filters because:  (1) it is unclear how the EyeLink machine is specifying their low-pass filter, and  (2) it conflicts with an assumption here in `eyeris::detransient()` to use one-step  difference to compute a threshold for detecting large jumps in pupil data  (suggesting blinking or other artifacts).   ***GENERAL TIP***  You should aim to have your data as raw as possible so you can 'cook' it fresh!   ***WHAT TO DO NEXT***  If you would like to continue preprocessing your current pupil data file,  you should consider skipping the `eyeris::detransient()` step of the pipeline altogether.  Advanced users might consider additional testing by manually passing in different `mad_thresh` override values  into `eyeris::detransient()` and then carefully assessing the consequences of any given override value on the pupil data;  however, this step is not recommended for most users.   PLEASE CONTINUE AT YOUR OWN RISK.

code: winsorize_pupil <- function(x, prev_op, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   vec <- x[[prev_op]]   q <- quantile(vec, probs = c(lower, upper), na.rm = TRUE)   vec[vec < q[1]] <- q[1]   vec[vec > q[2]] <- q[2]   vec }

text: eyeris object class eyeris dervived load(). n constant used compute median absolute deviation (MAD) threshold. mad_thresh Default NULL. parameter provides alternative options handling edge cases computed properties within detransient()  \(mad\_val\) \(median\_speed\) small. example, $$mad\_val = 0 \quad \text{} \quad median\_speed = 1,$$ , default multiplier \(n = 16\), $$mad\_thresh = median\_speed + (n \times mad\_val) = 1 + (16 \times 0) = 1.$$ situation, speed \(p_i \ge 1\) flagged transient, might overly sensitive. reduce sensitivity, two possible adjustments available: \(mad\_thresh = 1\), transient detection criterion modified $$p_i \ge mad\_thresh$$ $$p_i > mad\_thresh .$$ \(mad\_thresh\) small, user may manually adjust sensitivity supplying alternative threshold value directly via mad_thresh parameter.

title: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient
text: Computed properties: pupil_speed: Compute speed pupil approximating derivative x (pupil) respect y (time) using finite differences. Let \(x = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)\) \(y = (y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)\) two numeric vectors \(n \ge 2\); , finite differences computed : $$\delta_i = \frac{x_{+1} - x_i}{y_{+1} - y_i},      \quad = 1, 2, \dots, n-1.$$ produces output vector \(p = (p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n)\) defined : first element: $$p_1 = |\delta_1|,$$ last element: $$p_n = |\delta_{n-1}|,$$ intermediate elements (\(= 2, 3, \dots, n-1\)): $$p_i = \max\{|\delta_{-1}|,\,|\delta_i|\}.$$ median_speed: median computed pupil_speed: $$median\_speed = median(p)$$ mad_val: median absolute deviation (MAD) pupil_speed median: $$mad\_val = median(|p - median\_speed|)$$ mad_thresh: threshold computed median speed MAD, using constant multiplier \(n\) (default value: 16): $$mad\_thresh = median\_speed + (n \times mad\_val)$$
